item.title: MiBeeSteward v0.2.0: Distributed Discovery and Change Detection
item.description:
When v0.1.0 shipped, I wrote that it answers three questions: what devices are on the network, what they are, and how they relate. Honestly, v0.1.0 only answered the first half well — and only for the one LAN the center sat on.

The real-world layout is messier: one subnet in the office, one in the server room, another at home for test machines. The center lives in the office and literally cannot see the cameras in the server room. Getting it to scan the server room means crossing subnets — either opening up SNMP routing or just moving the center over there. Neither is elegant.

item.title: MiBeeSteward v0.3.0: Topology, Certificates, and Containers
item.description:
Take over an unfamiliar LAN and the first thing you need is to figure out what’s on it — office, server room, and home subnets tangled together, no documentation left behind, a switch full of MACs nobody can name. MiBeeSteward exists for exactly that: scan the network and tell you what devices are there, what they are, and how they connect.

v0.3.0 goes after three specific pains left over from the last two releases:

item.title: MiBeeSteward v0.4.0: Discovery on the Router Itself
item.description:
Finding out what lives on your LAN used to mean active scanning — traffic, blind spots — or running in a container, which needed host networking just to see the full device table. Meanwhile the router knows everything already, and the discovery system was walking around it.

Live on the router, everything visible

  • The discovery program runs on the router itself: who joined the WiFi, who got which IP, who is online right now — the router already knows, so it just reads
  • No port scanning, no probe traffic; the full device list appears quietly
  • OpenWrt installs and runs as a first-class citizen

A more trustworthy device ledger

  • A device changing IP no longer forks into “old and new” phantom entries
  • One authoritative record per device; history stops diverging

The gateway already knows everything — just ask it.
